def normalize(values):
    """Scale values linearly to [0, 1]: the minimum becomes 0.0, the maximum 1.0.

    If all values are equal, return a list of 0.0.
    An empty input returns an empty list.
    """
    lo, hi = min(values), max(values)
    return [(v - lo) / (hi - lo) for v in values]

The bug lies in the normalization logic. When all the values in the list are the same, `hi - lo` results in zero, causing a `ZeroDivisionError`. 

To fix this, we should handle the case where all values are equal by returning a list of zeros of the same length as the input list. 

I will make this change and then re-run the tests.
